newsitem.title: GERMANY: German call money steady at 3.05/3.06 pct.
newsitem.headline: German call money steady at 3.05/3.06 pct.

text.p: German call money traded steadily at 3.05 to 3.06 percent on Wednesday as the market took a relaxed view of the Bundesbank's move to drain one billion marks in funds at its weekly tender.
Dealers said liquidity conditions were strong, making the drain no problem whatsoever for the market.

Dealers also viewed with scepticism the speculation from abroad that the German central bank may be considering switching to a variable rate securities repurchase rate from the current fixed rate. There was no fundamental reason for a rate rise, one dealer said.
Such a move would leave with Bundesbank "with just secondary control" of interest rates, the dealer said.
"The psychological impact alone (of a variable rate repo) seems to me to be undesirable. Anyway at times like this strength comes from calm," he added.

Other dealers said a rise in short term interest rates would quickly affect long term market rates, and noted that several Bundesbank officials had stressed the importance of low market rates as a basis for economic growth.
Ample liquidity offset the impact of the Bundesbank's drain of funds at its weekly tender.
The Bundesbank allocated 77.9 billion marks in securities repurchase funds, replacing a repo pact for 78.9 billion.
Bank deposits with the central bank fell to 41.5 billion marks on Tuesday from 41.6 billion marks while the monthly average was unchanged at 41.3 billion. Lombard borrowings were negligible.
The Frankfurt Interbank Overnight Average was at 3.07575 percent on Wednesday (vs 3.08225 percent).
